explanations.silhouette:
This kiwi is a circle 14 pixels across. Circles get harder as they grow, so take your time: block it in the light brown and check that the edge steps the same way on all four sides.

![Silhouette](examples/silhouette.png) ![The finished kiwi](examples/finished.png)
explanations.outline:
A circle in pixels is built from runs that shrink toward the diagonals and grow toward the flat sides. Here that is 4 pixels across the top, then runs of 2, then single steps, then a straight run of 4 down each side. The same pattern repeats in every quarter.

A few outline pixels inside mark the edge of the green patch on the upper left.

![The outline on its own](examples/outline.png)
explanations.base:
Two base colors for two materials: light brown for the fuzzy skin and green for the patch on the upper left.

![Outline and base](examples/flat.png)
explanations.shadow:
The light comes from the top left. The brown darkens down the right side and across the bottom, in a band that is thickest at the bottom, where the fruit turns furthest from the light. The green takes a darker green along its lower edge.

![Flat](examples/flat.png) ![With shadow](examples/shaded.png)
explanations.highlight:
A white spot in the green is the shine. A lighter green along the top of the patch and pale pixels where the green meets the brown give it a rim that catches the light.

![With shadow](examples/shaded.png) ![With the highlights](examples/finished.png)
